propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref in S3, git ls-remote returns the ref at two SHAs and a fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable.

The upstream git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocks on input() at EOF in autonomous environments) and discards the non-chosen bundle head, causing permanent loss of events unique to that head in an append-only event store.
The current push path stalls because git-remote-s3 cmd_push rejects all ref operations while len(bundles)>1, and the subsequent fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, so retries never converge.

The heal must write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any original bundle and never delete the merged tip, ensuring at least one bundle carrying the full merged history remains remotely at every crash point.

The heal must fold N divergent bundle heads via iterated 2-parent lossless merges (not octopus merge), reusing rebar's existing sync reconcile semantics, and must abort without deleting if a genuine content conflict (non-derived file) is detected.

The doctor uses the helper's own S3Remote, acquire_lock/release_lock, get_bundles_for_ref, and boto3 client imported lazily, adding no direct S3 SDK dependency to core rebar and routing all S3 access through a single thin adapter.
